concerns.concern: The central claim is that gate cycling aligns polar nanoregions (PNRs) and leaves remnant polarization, which light then erases. None of this is measured directly: there are no C–V/P–E hysteresis, depolarization-current or SHG data, and no dielectric response before versus after gating or illumination.
concerns.quote: The cartoon in Fig. 3e ("PNRs pointing outwards/inwards") is therefore a hypothesis, not a result.

concerns.concern: A well-established competing explanation is neither addressed nor cited. Electrons escaping over the confining-potential edge into traps, as in LAO/STO back-gate hysteresis, combined with field-dependent permittivity, could explain the persistent R_s and mobility changes without PNRs.
concerns.quote: The relevant literature (e.g., Biscaras et al. and related works on STO back-gate hysteresis) is neither cited nor discussed.

concerns.concern: The authors do not test whether T_c is simply a single-valued function of R_s or mobility across both gating and illumination. If it is, carrier distribution, confinement and disorder explain the data and the PNR role is unnecessary. Prior KTO(111) studies already report T_c anticorrelating with mobility, so the result is less counterintuitive than presented.
concerns.quote: If T_c is single-valued in R_s or μ, the data are explained by changes in carrier distribution/confinement and disorder.

concerns.concern: "Complete erasure" is not shown against the pristine, pre-gating state at the same temperature and conditions. Pristine and illuminated resistances are quoted at different temperatures. The system does not fully recover, and the link between light erasure and room-temperature thermal reset is unclear.
concerns.quote: never compares L₄ to the virgin, pre-gating transition at the same temperature and measurement conditions.

concerns.concern: The T_c shifts are small (about 0.05–0.07 K) and defined at the 50% R_n criterion while R_n itself changes. Without alternative criteria, transition-width, BKT or H_c2 analysis, the shift may reflect inhomogeneity or percolation rather than pairing strength.
concerns.quote: No alternative criteria (onset, 10/90%, zero resistance) or analyses of transition width, BKT temperature or H_c2 are provided.

concerns.concern: The assignment of the ~30 K loss peak to PNRs rests on analogy with Li- or impurity-doped KTO. The substrates' impurity content is not characterized.
concerns.quote: The impurity content (Li, Fe, Na, etc.) of the substrates is not characterized.

concerns.concern: The 236 meV peak is assigned to oxygen-vacancy ionization only because its energy falls in a literature window. Other processes with similar energies are not excluded: defect-dipole complexes, hopping in the reduced layer, or Maxwell–Wagner interfacial relaxation.
concerns.quote: Other thermally activated processes with similar energies have not been excluded

concerns.concern: The linear relation between loop size and permittivity over about ten points does not establish causation, because both vary monotonically with temperature. The steeper slope below 35 K could instead reflect trap freezing or field-dependent ε.
concerns.quote: a linear Δ_L–ε relation between 95 and 35 K (roughly ten points) does not by itself establish causation.

concerns.concern: The claim that 1.97 eV photons randomize PNR orientations has no microscopic pathway. Local heating or photo-screening must be considered instead.
concerns.quote: Photon energy is not a natural variable for dipole reorientation, so local heating or photo-screening must be considered.

concerns.concern: All data appear to come from a single device, with no statement on sample number, batch variation or AlOₓ thickness. Controls are also missing: a non-superconducting or differently reduced KTO 2DEG, a (001) orientation, or an un-reduced substrate.
concerns.quote: All data appear to come from a single device. There is no statement on the number of samples, batch-to-batch variation or AlOₓ thickness.

concerns.concern: Error bars and sample-to-sample statistics are absent for the key superconducting results.
concerns.quote: Error bars and sample-to-sample statistics are absent.

concerns.concern: Carrier density and mobility come from single-band Hall analysis. Multiband conduction, expected for KTO(111) at these densities, could make the small extracted changes partly artefactual.
concerns.quote: Multiband conduction is expected for KTO(111) 2DEGs at n ~10¹⁴ cm⁻². It could make the extracted Δn and Δμ partly artefactual.

concerns.concern: The Hall-derived fractional changes are small (1–4%), yet run-to-run reproducibility and uncertainties are not reported.
concerns.quote: The fractional changes are small (Δn/n ~1–2%, Δμ/μ ~4%), but run-to-run reproducibility and uncertainties are not reported.

concerns.concern: The sample-temperature rise during illumination at 10 K is not quantified, although heating is visible at 2 K. Both persistent photoconductivity and the activation processes are strongly temperature dependent.
concerns.quote: Heating is visible at 2 K (resistance jumps), but the sample-temperature excursion at 10 K is not quantified.

concerns.concern: The capacitive charge expected from ε, the substrate thickness and the gate sweep should be compared quantitatively with the Hall-measured density change. Any discrepancy would be informative about trapping.
concerns.quote: should be compared quantitatively with the Hall Δn. If there is a discrepancy, it is itself informative about trapping.

concerns.concern: Permittivity was measured only at zero dc bias, although KTO's ε is strongly field-dependent within the gate range used.
concerns.quote: ε was measured only at zero dc bias, although ε(E) in KTO is strongly field-dependent within the ±50 V range used.

concerns.concern: The measured low-temperature permittivity (≈1600) is well below typical bulk KTO values, and the discrepancy is not discussed. Possible causes include the excitation amplitude, geometry or fringe corrections, a dead layer, or the reduced region.
concerns.quote: The measured ε ≈ 1600 at low T is well below typical bulk KTO values. The source of the discrepancy is not discussed

concerns.concern: The novelty claim is overstated. Gate-history T_c enhancement (Ref. 30), first-cycle back-gate hysteresis and persistent photoconductivity in KTO are already known. The advance beyond Ref. 30 needs to be stated clearly.
concerns.quote: The novelty claim ("previously unrecognized interplay") should be calibrated accordingly.

concerns.concern: No retention-time measurements at base temperature and no endurance data over many cycles are given. Both are essential for the non-volatile memory claim.
concerns.quote: No retention-time measurements at base temperature and no endurance data over many cycles are given.

concerns.concern: The neuromorphic and quantum-memristor framing lacks device-level metrics such as speed, energy, distinguishable levels and endurance. Programming with ±50 V and long illumination is impractical.
concerns.quote: The neuromorphic/quantum-memristor framing is not supported by device-level metrics.

concerns.concern: Photon flux and intensity at the sample are unknown. The LED is driven at a fixed voltage despite its temperature-dependent I–V characteristic.
concerns.quote: Photon flux and intensity at the sample are unknown; the LED is driven at fixed V_L

concerns.concern: Only one wavelength is used, so no spectral threshold is available to identify the defect levels responsible for erasure.
concerns.quote: Only one wavelength is used, so no spectral threshold is available to identify the defect levels involved.

concerns.concern: The fitted attempt frequencies of the two loss peaks are not reported, although they would help discriminate between mechanisms.
concerns.quote: The fitted prefactors ω₁, ω₂ (attempt frequencies) are not reported, although they would help discriminate between mechanisms.

concerns.concern: There is no quantitative model that reproduces the sign and magnitude of the R_s, density and mobility changes. An example would be trap/vacancy rate equations coupled to Schrödinger–Poisson confinement with field-dependent ε.
concerns.quote: Develop at least a minimal quantitative model ... that reproduces the sign and magnitude of the ΔR_s, Δn and Δμ changes.

concerns.concern: The dark-relaxation explanation invokes partially aligned PNRs and ionized vacancies in an interfacial trap without a model. The non-monotonic time constant could arise from overlapping relaxations, which a two-component fit should test.
concerns.quote: The non-monotonic τ(T) could arise from overlapping relaxations with different amplitudes. A two-component fit would test this.

concerns.concern: The claim that electrons tunnel back to deep donors beyond −17 V is asserted rather than tested, for example via its temperature or sweep-rate dependence.
concerns.quote: This is asserted rather than tested, for example by its temperature or sweep-rate dependence.

concerns.concern: The Type A/B sequence dependence is presented as an additional sensitivity. It appears simply to reflect which branch of the known hysteresis loop the sweep ends on.
concerns.quote: It appears simply to reflect which branch of the known hysteresis loop the sweep ends on

concerns.concern: The van der Pauw-to-sheet-resistance conversion via FEM, and possible transport anisotropy of KTO(111), are not documented.
concerns.quote: The van der Pauw-to-R_s conversion via FEM, and the possible anisotropy of KTO(111) transport (Ref. 16), should be documented.

concerns.concern: The Discussion contains a duplicated sentence about interactions being reinforced.
concerns.quote: A duplicated sentence appears in the Discussion ("The interactions are further reinforced… Dielectric loss signatures further reinforce…").

concerns.concern: There are notation, figure-naming and caption inconsistencies: R_s^b used where R_s^a is meant, "Extended" versus "Supplementary" Figure 5, and the Fig. 3 caption contradicting the main text.
concerns.quote: Supp. Note 4 labels the elevated value as "R_s^b = 856 Ω" when R_s^a is meant.

concerns.concern: The manuscript has misused terms and typographical errors, such as "variance" for "variation" and several misspellings.
concerns.quote: Misused terms: "variance" for "variation"; "illlumination", "memrisitive", "the it is", "would facilitates".
